phases.name: Repository Bootstrap
phases.goal: A master repository that builds, tests and documents itself, with every later phase already planned.

phases.name: Engineering Foundation
phases.goal: Any developer runs `make setup && make dev` and gets a working API, database, queue, websocket and admin panel.

phases.name: Design System & Mobile Shell
phases.goal: A navigable, themed app shell with a documented component library the rest of the client is built from.

phases.name: Identity & Authentication
phases.goal: A player can create an account, sign in on a device, stay signed in securely, and revoke other sessions.

phases.name: Player Profile & Onboarding
phases.goal: An authenticated account becomes a named player inside a chosen world, with a private realtime channel.

phases.name: World Architecture
phases.goal: A persistent, queryable world of regions and tiles that the client can read a viewport of without ever loading the whole map.

phases.name: World Map Rendering
phases.goal: A fluid, gesture-driven world map that stays at 60 FPS with thousands of entities on screen.

phases.name: City Foundation
phases.goal: A player owns a city with addressable building slots, rendered as a living scene rather than a list.

phases.name: Resources & Economy
phases.goal: Resources accrue over real time, are capped by storage, and can never be duplicated or spent twice.

phases.name: Buildings & Construction
phases.goal: A player queues building upgrades that cost resources, take server-controlled time, and complete reliably even if a worker dies.

phases.name: Technology & Research
phases.goal: A player researches technologies from an acyclic tree whose effects measurably modify their empire.

phases.name: Unit System
phases.goal: A complete, data-driven unit roster with stats and a counter system richer than rock-paper-scissors.

phases.name: Training System
phases.goal: A player trains troops in queues that cost resources and time and produce exactly the promised units.

phases.name: Heroes
phases.goal: Heroes exist as collectible, levelling commanders whose bonuses measurably change army and city outcomes.

phases.name: Army Composition
phases.goal: A player assembles named armies from garrison troops with a hero and formation, bounded by real capacity rules.

phases.name: March System
phases.goal: Armies move across the world over server-computed time, arrive reliably, and can be recalled.

phases.name: PvE World Encounters
phases.goal: The world holds NPC camps and resource nodes that give solo players something to do and a reason to march.

phases.name: Combat Engine V1
phases.goal: A deterministic battle simulator that produces identical results from identical inputs and stores a replayable, compact record.

phases.name: Battle Visualization
phases.goal: A player can see what happened in a battle and why, replayed from the compact server record.

phases.name: PvP
phases.goal: Players attack each other under rules that make aggression meaningful without letting veterans farm beginners.

phases.name: Siege & City Capture
phases.goal: Cities can be besieged and captured under rules that are decisive but reversible enough to keep a server alive.

phases.name: Territory System
phases.goal: Land ownership is a first-class, contestable resource rather than a cosmetic overlay.

phases.name: Alliances
phases.goal: Players form alliances with real internal authority expressed as permissions, not role-name string checks.

phases.name: Alliance Territory
phases.goal: Alliances hold and defend collective territory that confers shared benefits.

phases.name: Rally & Reinforcements
phases.goal: Alliance members combine armies into a single rally attack or reinforce each other's cities.

phases.name: Chat & Social
phases.goal: Players communicate across scoped channels with rate limiting, blocking and an auditable trail.

phases.name: Diplomacy
phases.goal: Alliances hold formal relationships that change what their members are allowed to do to each other.

phases.name: Market & Trading
phases.goal: Resources move between players through trades that are taxed, rate-limited and impossible to duplicate.

phases.name: Quests & Achievements
phases.goal: Players always have a next objective, from the first minute of the tutorial to long-term achievements.

phases.name: Nobility
phases.goal: A visible social ladder that rewards sustained play with status and concrete privileges.

phases.name: Rankings
phases.goal: Players can see where they stand on leaderboards that are fast, paginated and auditable.

phases.name: Events & LiveOps
phases.goal: Operators launch, modify and end timed events and toggle features entirely from the back office.

phases.name: Seasons
phases.goal: A world runs competitive seasons with their own rules, rankings and rewards.

phases.name: Notifications
phases.goal: Players are told what matters — an attack incoming, a build finished — and can control exactly what reaches them.

phases.name: Admin & Game Master Tools
phases.goal: Operators can inspect and correct any game state through tooling that records who did what, when and why.

phases.name: Moderation
phases.goal: Abuse can be reported, reviewed and acted on with a complete evidence trail.

phases.name: Analytics
phases.goal: Product events flow to analytics without any gameplay path depending on the analytics pipeline.

phases.name: Security & Anti-Cheat Hardening
phases.goal: Every threat in the threat model has either a control or a documented, accepted risk.

phases.name: Performance Optimization
phases.goal: The game meets its stated performance budget on both server and device, measured rather than asserted.

phases.name: Load Testing
phases.goal: Capacity claims are backed by reproducible measurements rather than optimism.

phases.name: Offline & Connectivity Resilience
phases.goal: A player on a bad connection sees honest state and never performs a server-authoritative action that silently fails.

phases.name: Accessibility
phases.goal: The game is playable by people who need larger text, higher contrast, less motion or a screen reader.

phases.name: Localization
phases.goal: Every player-visible string comes from a translation catalogue in the player's language.

phases.name: Audio & Haptics
phases.goal: Actions feel physical through layered sound and haptics the player can turn off.

phases.name: Visual Polish
phases.goal: The game looks and feels like a commercial product rather than a themed CRUD app.

phases.name: Tutorial & FTUE Polish
phases.goal: A brand-new player understands the game and reaches their first meaningful win without external help.

phases.name: Economy Balance Pass
phases.goal: The economy is tuned against simulation rather than intuition, with sinks that actually absorb supply.

phases.name: Combat Balance Pass
phases.goal: No single composition dominates, and the counter system rewards thought rather than raw numbers.

phases.name: Closed Alpha
phases.goal: A small invited group plays a real server and their problems are captured and triaged.

phases.name: Beta
phases.goal: A larger population plays continuously while the team watches the metrics that matter and can ship a fix quickly.

phases.name: Production Infrastructure
phases.goal: Production infrastructure is reproducible from code and its recovery procedures have actually been tested.

phases.name: Store Release Pipeline
phases.goal: A signed build reaches both stores through a repeatable pipeline with a safe rollback path.

phases.name: Launch Readiness
phases.goal: Every launch prerequisite is verified and signed off, with named owners for the first days.

phases.name: Global Launch
phases.goal: The game is publicly available and the first worlds open under active monitoring.

phases.name: Post-launch LiveOps
phases.goal: The game runs as a live service with a repeatable rhythm for content, balance and player health.
